topics.name: Sense words: looks / sounds / smells / feels / tastes + adjective

questions.rule: After sense verbs like tastes, use an adjective: tastes sweet. One mango takes -s.
owl starts with a vowel sound, so use an. 'an' goes with one thing only.

options: The kitten is looking at a ball.
The kitten is look at a ball.
The kitten are looking at a ball.
questions.rule: Present continuous = is + verb-ing. One kitten takes is: is looking.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After feels, use an adjective, not an -ly adverb: feels soft and warm.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A daily habit with one person (Grandma) takes the simple present with -s: lights.
After tastes, use an adjective to describe the taste: tastes sour.
elephant starts with a vowel sound and is one animal, so use an.
Present continuous: subject + is + verb-ing. loudly tells how.
With it, add -s: tastes. After a sense verb, use an adjective: yummy.
In a 'yes' (positive) sentence, use some. With we, use have.

options: There isn't some noise in the room.
There aren't any noise in the room.
There isn't any noise in the room.
questions.rule: In negative sentences use any. Noise cannot be counted, so use isn't.

options: The photograph show a tiny black kitten.
The photograph shows a tiny black kitten.
The photograph showing a tiny black kitten.
questions.rule: The photograph is one thing, so the simple present verb takes -s: shows.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two sisters is plural, so use are: are singing.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After smell, use an adjective: the eggs smell bad.
In a negative sentence (do not), use any.
loud starts with a consonant sound, so use a: a loud honk.
feels + adjectives: the sand feels hot and dry.
In questions, use any: Are there any mangoes?

chat: What can you see in the picture?
options: I can see a owl on a branch.
I can see an owl on a branch.
I can see an owl on an branch.
questions.rule: an before a vowel sound (an owl), a before a consonant sound (a branch).

options: She is playing with a rattle.
She is play with a rattle.
questions.rule: Present continuous needs is + verb-ing: she is playing.

options: The old rope feels roughly and hard.
The old rope feels rough and hard.
The old rope feel rough and hard.
questions.rule: feels + adjectives: rough and hard. The rope is one thing, so the verb takes -s.

options: An umbrella is lying on the wet grass.
A umbrella is lying on the wet grass.
An umbrella are lying on the wet grass.
questions.rule: umbrella starts with a vowel sound: an. One umbrella takes is.

options: Is there any frogs near the lake?
Are there any frog near the lake?
Are there any frogs near the lake?
questions.rule: Questions use any. Frogs is plural, so use Are there + a plural noun.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Smoke cannot be counted, so it takes is: is curling.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The Godavari is one river, so the simple present verb takes -s: flows.
After smells, use an adjective: smells delicious.
In a positive sentence, use some: bought some vegetables.
An before the vowel sound of owl; the dark = a particular darkness we know.
In a negative sentence (isn't), use any: there isn't any left.
With it, add -s: sounds. After a sense verb, use adjectives: sweet and soft.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Yesterday the market smells of fresh mangoes.
Yesterday the market smelled of fresh mangoes.
Yesterday the market smelling of fresh mangoes.
questions.rule: Yesterday shows the past, so use the past form: smelled.

options: We saw an huge elephant at the zoo.
We saw a huge elephant at the zoo.
We seen a huge elephant at the zoo.
questions.rule: huge starts with a consonant sound: a huge elephant. Past of see is saw.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Sheep is the same in singular and plural: one sheep, two sheep.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Comparing two things with than needs the -er form: feels softer than.
old starts with a vowel sound, so use an: an old fort.
Some sweets is plural, so use the plural verb were.
tasted (past) + adjective: tasted too salty.
Present continuous: is hiding. under tells the place.

chat: What did you see at the station?
options: I saw a engine and a long train.
I saw an engine and a long train.
I see an engine and a long train.
questions.rule: an engine (vowel sound), a long train. The question is past, so use saw.
With it, add -s: opens. Use at for a clock time.

options: The rain is falling softly, and the wet earth smells fresh.
The rain is falling softly, and the wet earth smell fresh.
The rain are falling softly, and the wet earth smells fresh.
questions.rule: The rain takes is; the earth (one thing) takes smells + adjective fresh.

options: An eagle is flying high above the hills.
A eagle is flying high above the hills.
An eagle is fly high above the hills.
questions.rule: eagle starts with a vowel sound: an eagle. Present continuous: is flying.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A habit (always) with one person (my brother) takes -s: whispers, like sleeps.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After looks, use adjectives: looks green and fresh.
Look! = happening now. Two butterflies is plural: are fluttering.

questions.after: old bus woke the whole street.
questions.rule: old begins with a vowel sound, so use an: an old bus.
Nobody makes the sentence negative, so use any: making any noise.
Adjective before the noun (sticky honey), and adjective after the sense verb (tastes very sweet).

chat: Did you hear any sounds in the forest?
options: Yes, I heard any birds and a loud crash.
Yes, I heard some birds and a loud crash.
Yes, I hear some birds and a loud crash.
questions.rule: A positive answer uses some. The question is past (did), so use heard.

chat: What does your grandmother do every evening?
options: She light a lamp and sings softly.
She lights a lamp and sing softly.
She lights a lamp and sings softly.
questions.rule: A daily habit with she: both verbs take -s: lights and sings.
